name: Argentina

eSignLaw.name: Digital Signature Law 25.506 and the Civil and Commercial Code
eSignLaw.citation: Ley 25.506; Civil and Commercial Code arts. 286-288

levelNote: An electronic signature is valid, but if its authenticity is disputed the person relying on it must prove it. A digital signature with a certificate is presumed authentic.

formRequirements.note: Wills must follow the formalities of the Civil and Commercial Code (handwritten or by public deed).
Property transfers need a public deed (escritura publica).

notices: Electronic signature law that applies: Digital Signature Law 25.506 and the Civil and Commercial Code. An electronic signature is valid, but if its authenticity is disputed the person relying on it must prove it. A digital signature with a certificate is presumed authentic.
You must be at least 18 years old to sign this agreement.
If you are unsure whether this applies to you, ask for a paper alternative before signing.
limitationNote: General period: five years (Civil and Commercial Code art. 2560); consumer claims: three.

sources.title: Argentine legislation portal (search: Ley 25.506 firma digital)
